title: Optimizing Investment Alpha with Customized Completion Portfolios Featuring Chris Jones, Ph.D.

speakers: Chris Jones (Graham Capital, head of London office, client solutions)
Ella (former BCI total fund management lead, institutional adviser)
summary: Panel on customized managed accounts and completion portfolios for institutional allocators. Covers move from strategic asset allocation to total portfolio approach, building bespoke hedge-fund/CTA sleeves (beta caps, vol targets, hybrid strategies), ESG futures, and why equity-bond correlation risk in inflation drives demand for downside-diversifying completion funds.

claims.speaker: Judy Posnikoff
claims.quote: we moved to doing funds of one um and that's where a lot of the customization really came in
claims.claim: Allocators moved from share classes of manager funds to funds of one to get bespoke terms, leverage, concentration or removal of exposures, which is the first step of customization.
claims.testable: no - industry history, not a tradable rule

claims.speaker: Judy Posnikoff
claims.quote: we would have a Quant fund that was really good but you know returns were probably in the low um single digits and so we would add leverage in that share class
claims.claim: Good but low-return quant funds were made useful by adding leverage in a dedicated share class, so the allocator scaled return to target.
claims.direction: add leverage to a low-vol quant fund
claims.conditions: when the strategy is good but its return is too low for the allocator's target
claims.testable: partly - leverage scaling of a strategy can be backtested

claims.speaker: Judy Posnikoff
claims.quote: the managers did the trading but we did all of the back office and everything there
claims.claim: An internal managed-account platform gives the allocator control of the portfolio and scale efficiencies with prime brokers and counterparties while managers only trade.

claims.speaker: Ella
claims.quote: the reason why smas were really um uh favorable is because investors wanted to own the assets in segregated fashion
claims.claim: Separately managed accounts became favored because investors wanted to own assets segregated, a preference reinforced after the GFC when managers failed and portfolio construction burden fell on investors.

claims.speaker: Ella
claims.quote: it was the law for long environment where there was an extended Equity bull market that anything that competed with equities look dismal
claims.claim: A long equity bull market made anything competing with equities look poor, which pushed allocators to find new ways of building portfolios and thus customization.

claims.speaker: Ella
claims.quote: a big chunk of the alpha uh became Beta And if Alpha is a zero sum game too many managers chasing it
claims.claim: As asset management proliferated, much former alpha became cheap beta and alpha is zero-sum with too many managers chasing it, making alpha harder and costlier to harvest.
claims.testable: partly - alpha decay could be tested on manager returns

claims.speaker: Ella
claims.quote: lastly was the move towards total fund or total portfolio approach which was all about portfolio construction
claims.claim: The shift to a total fund approach moved value added from manager selection to total-portfolio construction, which also drives customization.

claims.speaker: Ella
claims.quote: the active management will be relatively more difficult on the upside so manager selection I think will lose its significance in portfolio construction
claims.claim: If the equity bull market continues, active managers struggle to add on the upside so manager selection matters less and index-type beta strategies grow.
claims.direction: more index beta, fewer active managers

claims.speaker: Ella
claims.quote: only those managers and providers who can actually be integrated into the portfolio teams internal teams that can team up and be an extension of these teams will survive it
claims.claim: Surviving managers will be those who integrate with allocators' internal teams as an extension of them, since the fee pie available to managers shrinks.

claims.speaker: Ella
claims.quote: if the there's a decent correction in the markets or there is a decoupling then the manager selection will have a renewed importance in the institutional portfolio
claims.claim: In the alternative scenario of a decent market correction or decoupling, manager selection regains importance and customization progresses more slowly.
claims.conditions: after a market correction or decoupling

claims.speaker: Ella
claims.quote: today if you look at any SMA you're not going to get in if you're even 50 million because it's not really worth right the effort
claims.claim: Minimum useful size for a separately managed account rose from under 4 million in the 2000s to above 50 million now, showing the industry matured.

claims.speaker: Chris Jones
claims.quote: it was turning a dial it was uh maybe having a higher V Target for Capital efficiency
claims.claim: First-stage customization of managed accounts was simple dial turning such as a higher volatility target, a foreign-currency account or excluding a few markets, so that the manager fits the rest of the portfolio.
claims.direction: raise vol target to fit portfolio
claims.testable: yes - vol-target variants of a strategy can be backtested

claims.speaker: Chris Jones
claims.quote: we found the much more effective way to do this than just removing upside Equity exposure was to cap the beta overall in the portfolio so that Equity uh exposure doesn't pop up in Commodities or or elsewhere
claims.claim: To limit equity exposure in a CTA, capping the overall portfolio beta is more effective than removing equity markets, because equity risk otherwise reappears through commodities and other markets.
claims.direction: cap equity beta of the whole portfolio
claims.conditions: trend/CTA portfolios where equity risk leaks into other markets
claims.testable: yes - beta cap can be applied in backtest

claims.speaker: Chris Jones
claims.quote: investors really viewed for right or wrong hedge funds as an asset class
claims.claim: In the 2000s boards allocated to hedge funds as one asset class with little strategy-level customization; post-GFC investors began specifying which strategies they wanted.

claims.speaker: Chris Jones
claims.quote: the last stages the portfolio construction architecture the constraints the optimization the risk overlay and so uh because this is the last stage you can put in any sensible constraint or cap and still end up with an optimal portfolio
claims.claim: Because constraints, optimization and risk overlay are the last stage of a quant process, any sensible cap can be built into the optimization and yield an optimal constrained portfolio rather than a suboptimal remnant.
claims.conditions: quant systematic macro where portfolio construction is the final stage
claims.testable: yes - constrained optimization can be backtested vs ex-post removal

claims.speaker: Chris Jones
claims.quote: you can net the signals and have an optimal portfolio there
claims.claim: Hybridizing strategies by netting their signals before portfolio construction gives an optimal combined book and the beta cap need not be zero but can be set to whatever fits the client portfolio.
claims.testable: yes - signal netting vs separate sleeves is testable

claims.speaker: Chris Jones
claims.quote: working out what's that Gap in the client's portfolio and what's the best fit for it
claims.claim: A completion portfolio first identifies the gap in the client's existing portfolio and then designs the best-fit exposure, an outcome-oriented rather than strategy-selection approach.
claims.testable: partly - fit to a gap can be measured vs the existing portfolio

claims.speaker: Chris Jones
claims.quote: it's so easy to to to O over optimize that it's important I think to have that honest relationship with the clients
claims.claim: Customized portfolios are easy to over-optimize, so robustness requires an honest discussion with clients about what is achievable and what pushes the fit too far.
claims.testable: partly - overfitting can be tested out of sample

claims.speaker: Chris Jones
claims.quote: we can add uh uh uh optimal baskets of assets we can add volatility exposure
claims.claim: Completion portfolios can combine the manager's alpha strategies with optimal baskets of assets and volatility exposure, tailored to the role needed in the client's portfolio.
claims.testable: partly - components are testable, combination is bespoke

claims.speaker: Stephanie Freeze
claims.quote: close to over 60% are using or offering customized Solutions
claims.claim: A live poll of the webinar audience (half fund managers, a quarter investors) showed about 50% use strategic asset allocation and over 60% use or offer customized solutions.

claims.speaker: Judy Posnikoff
claims.quote: you're talking about generalists in most cases rather than Specialists
claims.claim: A total fund approach changes organization: senior staff are generalists who think about the overall portfolio rather than their own asset-class bucket.

claims.speaker: Judy Posnikoff
claims.quote: you tend not to have as many external managers as you do with the um strategic asset allocation approach
claims.claim: Total fund portfolios hold fewer external managers because exposures that overlap across asset-class buckets are visible and need not be duplicated.
claims.testable: partly - overlap across managers is measurable

claims.speaker: Judy Posnikoff
claims.quote: there's more of an opportunity to use um overlays with the total fund approach you know um options in some cases risk mitigation strategies
claims.claim: A total fund view lets an allocator target portfolio-level holes with overlays, options and risk-mitigation strategies, whereas under SAA fixing them means taking money from one bucket and creates internal political pressure.

claims.speaker: Judy Posnikoff
claims.quote: the large investors that have moved towards the total fund approach have reported significant Savings in the investment costs
claims.claim: Large investors using a total fund approach report significant cost savings from fewer, larger manager relationships with better fee terms.
claims.testable: partly - fee and cost data are measurable

claims.speaker: Judy Posnikoff
claims.quote: so you get I think broader and hopefully more um participatory decision-making there with the total fund approach
claims.claim: Total fund management gives broader participatory decision-making because the whole portfolio is discussed together instead of being passed up through layers.

claims.speaker: Ella
claims.quote: looks at the long-term capital Market assumptions say 12% for Equity 6% for bonds Etc considers a long-term return Target for a specific plan looks at the funded status volatility
claims.claim: Strategic asset allocation takes long-term capital market assumptions, a return target and funded status volatility and outputs an asset mix, which works well with few asset classes and small internal teams.
claims.conditions: limited internal teams, few asset classes

claims.speaker: Ella
claims.quote: Trend fallowing you can actually get it as beta um and um only very differentiated managers are worth the cost of 20 220
claims.claim: Trend following can now be obtained as cheap beta, so only very differentiated managers justify 2 and 20 fees.
claims.direction: use trend beta instead of paying alpha fees
claims.testable: yes - trend replication vs manager returns net of fees is testable

claims.speaker: Ella
claims.quote: SAA is really driven by uh benchmarks per asset class and it's all about beating those benchmarks
claims.claim: SAA is driven by asset-class benchmarks that managers aim to beat by 50 to 100 bps, whereas total portfolio approach is holistic and judged on the whole portfolio.

claims.speaker: Ella
claims.quote: you're looking at macroeconomic risk factors such as inflation real rates uh credit Etc
claims.claim: A total portfolio approach organizes the portfolio by macro risk factors (inflation, real rates, credit) and treats asset classes as secondary labels.
claims.indicator: inflation, real rates, credit risk factors
claims.testable: partly - factor exposures can be estimated

claims.speaker: Ella
claims.quote: the asset classes or teams um basically uh compete for Capital so all investment opportunities are competing
claims.claim: In TPA all investment opportunities compete for capital on their contribution to the whole portfolio rather than filling asset-class buckets.
claims.direction: capital allocated to best marginal contribution
claims.testable: partly - marginal contribution ranking is testable

claims.speaker: Ella
claims.quote: managers are hired on the basis that they improve the risk adjusted returns of the entire portfolio
claims.claim: Under TPA a manager must have a proposition strong enough to improve risk-adjusted return of the whole portfolio, not just one asset class.
claims.testable: yes - marginal Sharpe contribution is measurable

claims.speaker: Ella
claims.quote: it's really a total portfolio concept as its main role is to mitigate the draw down triggered by whatever the biggest risk in the total portfolio is
claims.claim: A risk-mitigation portfolio is defined by its role of cushioning the drawdown caused by the largest risk in the total portfolio, reducing the conditional beta to it and raising liquidity and dry powder dynamically.
claims.testable: partly - conditional beta and drawdown contribution are measurable

claims.speaker: Ella
claims.quote: that framework was set up to utilize a combination of passive and active strategies
claims.claim: The risk mitigation framework combines passive and active strategies, the active ones run by a handful of managers willing to structure strategies specifically for the allocator's portfolio.

claims.speaker: Chris Jones
claims.quote: with completion portfolios you have to sit on the same side of the table you have to work in Partnership
claims.claim: Completion portfolios invert the manager-investor relationship into a partnership where much time is spent formulating the problem before finding the solution.

claims.speaker: Chris Jones
claims.quote: it's less manager selection it's more kind of outcome selection I would say there's no best manager for this it's just which is the best fit for for my portfolio
claims.claim: Completion funds shift from manager selection to outcome selection: the best manager is the one whose output best fills the gap in the specific portfolio.

claims.speaker: Chris Jones
claims.quote: these constraints aren't necessarily portfolio constraints they could be governance constraints
claims.claim: Customization must reflect governance and other non-portfolio constraints as well as portfolio ones when formulating the optimization problem.

claims.speaker: Chris Jones
claims.quote: we're at our best I think when clients share with us their portfolio data so then we can kind of really uh uh build an optimal fit
claims.claim: Optimal completion design needs the client's actual portfolio data, although anonymized data or headline proxies can be used at earlier stages.

claims.speaker: Chris Jones
claims.quote: everybody's worried about kind of uh equities and bonds getting correlated everybody's worried about inflation
claims.claim: Concerns about stock-bond correlation turning positive and about inflation are universal across pension plans and wealth investors, so completion solutions are not limited to one client type.

claims.speaker: Judy Posnikoff
claims.quote: there are a lot of very very sophisticated smaller allocators out there or smaller um plans
claims.claim: Interest in completion-type customized solutions cannot be predicted by allocator size because many small plans are sophisticated.

claims.speaker: Ella
claims.quote: you'll see very small like very sophisticated but uh relatively small or midsize plans uh globally who are actually applying it
claims.claim: A peer review found total-portfolio management and risk mitigation are applied by relatively small and mid-size plans worldwide, not only the largest ones.

claims.speaker: Ella
claims.quote: I've seen one group actually doing internal uh a small group uh doing an internal trading to apply and to implement risk mitigation
claims.claim: A small internal team has implemented risk mitigation trading in-house with pretty good results, showing it can be done with limited resources.

claims.speaker: Judy Posnikoff
claims.quote: people are now started have started to get worried about what's called greenwashing
claims.claim: Investors increasingly worry about greenwashing, i.e. ESG labels that are not truly ESG, especially on the environmental side.

claims.speaker: Judy Posnikoff
claims.quote: what they found is that divestment hasn't worked as well as probably has been hoped
claims.claim: A Stanford paper on divestment found that excluding stocks from portfolios has not worked as well as investors working with companies to change their practices.

claims.speaker: Judy Posnikoff
claims.quote: a lot of the um environmental portfolios really outperformed but that was because they didn't include energy and that's obviously changed this year
claims.claim: Environmental portfolios outperformed until about this year only because they excluded energy; when energy rallied the performance flipped, so ESG performance is mostly a sector bet.
claims.direction: environmental funds outperform when energy lags, underperform when energy leads
claims.conditions: depends on energy sector relative performance
claims.testable: yes - ESG vs non-ESG returns decomposed by energy weight

claims.speaker: Judy Posnikoff
claims.quote: you don't get the sense that um it's always a good thing in terms of performance to exclude part of the investable universe
claims.claim: Excluding part of the investable universe is not reliably good for performance, which investors will have to grapple with.
claims.testable: partly - exclusion cost can be backtested

claims.speaker: Chris Jones
claims.quote: there's actually now the instruments available to start to implement uh on an ESG basis on the future side of things
claims.claim: ESG equity index futures are now available for systematic macro and trend followers to implement ESG preferences in futures.
claims.testable: partly - futures exist so a swap test is feasible

claims.speaker: Chris Jones
claims.quote: they've uh increased in open interest two to three times you know they're starting to get tradable now
claims.claim: The S&P ESG future and the Euro Stoxx 600 ESG future have grown open interest two to three times and are starting to be tradable.
claims.indicator: open interest of S&P ESG future and Euro Stoxx 600 ESG future

claims.speaker: Chris Jones
claims.quote: you could manage a portfolio of around 100 million so you know it's not a billion it's not 10 billion it's 100 million
claims.claim: Replacing all equity index futures exposure with the two most liquid ESG contracts would cap capacity at about 100 million while staying under 30% of open interest.
claims.testable: yes - capacity calculation from open interest

claims.speaker: Chris Jones
claims.quote: if you replace uh those uh uh standard Equity index Futures with their ESG counterparts you don't have any return drag
claims.claim: On a small, rudimentary data set swapping standard equity index futures for ESG counterparts showed no return drag, even a slight pickup.
claims.indicator: ESG vs standard equity index futures returns
claims.testable: yes - return comparison of two futures series

claims.speaker: Chris Jones
claims.quote: put that is as an optimization constraint
claims.claim: Client restrictions such as no grains or no fossil-fuel energy are handled as constraints in the portfolio optimization rather than as ad hoc deletions.

claims.speaker: Ella
claims.quote: there was nothing standardized and we grappled with the idea of does it add value
claims.claim: ESG ratings and frameworks are not standardized, so it is unclear whether ESG adds value or is mainly an exclusion.

claims.speaker: Ella
claims.quote: e seems to be taking over the S and the G and given the non-standardized analytics it's very difficult to calculate the potential impact
claims.claim: Environmental factors dominate S and G and, with non-standard analytics, ESG impact cannot be quantified consistently beyond simple exclusions like energy, grains or fossil fuels, so each institution builds its own factor framework.

claims.speaker: Ella
claims.quote: the idea is to break ESG into risk factors and it's the main risk factors whatever they might be macroeconomic and bundle it as such
claims.claim: Under a total fund approach ESG can be implemented by mapping it into the main macro risk factors and feeding them into portfolio optimization.

claims.speaker: Ella
claims.quote: it's not guaranteed that you're going to get better risk adjusted returns
claims.claim: ESG-based frameworks can lead to a different portfolio than intended and do not guarantee better risk-adjusted returns.

claims.speaker: Chris Jones
claims.quote: this was just a a 20-year free lunch we've had and in fact kind of equities and bonds can be positively correlated
claims.claim: The roughly 20-year negative equity-bond correlation may have been a free lunch, because stocks and bonds can be positively correlated for long periods.

claims.speaker: Chris Jones
claims.quote: the period of of of positive correlation uh which went from kind of the the kind of essentially ' 70s ' 80s '90s
claims.claim: Per Graham's CIO paper, stocks and bonds were positively correlated for about 30 years across the 1970s to 1990s, longer than the recent ~20 year negative correlation.

claims.speaker: Chris Jones
claims.quote: correlation between equities and bonds could be identified by hawkish fed policy and uh inflation shock essentially
claims.claim: Periods of positive stock-bond correlation can be identified by hawkish Fed policy and an inflation shock.
claims.indicator: hawkish Fed policy, inflation shock, stock-bond correlation
claims.testable: yes - regime test of correlation sign

claims.speaker: Chris Jones
claims.quote: if I've got a core a portfolio that's essentially 6 40 uh that used to naturally offset in terms of risk and now is all potentially going to drop like a stone together in a crisis
claims.claim: If stocks and bonds correlate positively, a 60/40 core loses its natural offset and drops together in a crisis, so investors seek diversification and loss control through completion funds, not necessarily using bonds.

claims.speaker: Judy Posnikoff
claims.quote: they find that equities do very poorly in an inflationary period
claims.claim: Old academic papers find equities do very poorly in inflationary periods.
claims.testable: yes - equity returns by inflation regime

claims.speaker: Judy Posnikoff
claims.quote: whether a particular company is going to benefit or be really hurt by you know Rising prices from Supply ERS and so forth and they don't have Market power
claims.claim: In inflation, deep fundamental research on which companies have pricing power versus supplier-cost pressure gives long/short equity managers an opportunity.
claims.indicator: pricing power vs input cost pressure
claims.direction: long pricing-power firms, short firms with no market power

claims.speaker: Judy Posnikoff
claims.quote: aqr just came out with a a paper on Trend following should do well in inflationary periods
claims.claim: An AQR paper argues trend following should do well in inflationary periods, though the speaker says it remains to be seen.
claims.testable: yes - CTA returns vs inflation regime

claims.speaker: Ella
claims.quote: I think infrastructure and certain inflation sensitive commodity so um for institutional investors with such inflation sensitive assets already in their portfolios great uh very well positioned
claims.claim: Investors already holding infrastructure and inflation-sensitive real assets are well positioned for inflation, but privates are limited and commodities are a single instrument, so more tools are needed.

claims.speaker: Ella
claims.quote: the uh risk parity managers that actually have um an inflation Focus
claims.claim: Risk parity managers with an inflation focus could be a good play for the inflationary period.
claims.testable: partly - risk parity variants are testable

claims.speaker: Ella
claims.quote: obviously linkers and uh gold if you prefer a more blunt object
claims.claim: Inflation-linked bonds and gold are standard instruments for inflation protection, with gold as the blunter tool.

claims.speaker: Ella
claims.quote: I think we're in inflation but I think it's not going to be permanent
claims.claim: View that the then-current inflation is not permanent, so the bigger issue is low returns and loss of insurance from government bonds.

claims.speaker: Ella
claims.quote: I think there's a decent chance that bonds may join equities on the downside in an inflationary environment
claims.claim: In an inflationary environment government bonds may fall together with equities, so bonds fail as insurance and risk-mitigation completion strategies become crucial.
claims.testable: yes - joint drawdowns in inflation regimes

claims.speaker: Chris Jones
claims.quote: there's definitely been a shift from looking for uncorrelated elements to put in the portfolio to elements that have a uh a a a downside diversification benefit
claims.claim: Investors now look for conditional (down-market) correlation and downside diversification rather than average low correlation.

claims.speaker: Ella
claims.quote: how do you actually offset the equity downturn conditional um beta reducing the uh uh the capture downside capture
claims.claim: Investors want to offset equity downturns through lower conditional beta and downside capture and are willing to pay active fees only for esoteric strategies that deliver this, preferring cheaper implementation otherwise.
